# `silk/cli/parse`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Parse a command line into a struct, and write the help text of a command.

## When to use
Call [`Cli.read`](#Cli.impl.read) from `main` to read the process arguments and print help, the version, or
errors, [`Cli.fromHost`](#Cli.impl.fromHost) to handle those yourself, or [`Cli.parse`](#Cli.impl.parse) to parse a list of
arguments that you already have, such as in a test.

## Details
The type to parse has `CommandLine`, which describes it. The description and the type are
checked against each other during compilation. The loops over the fields and variants are
expanded during compilation too, so the parser that runs only compares each argument with the
option names and calls the reader of the matching field type. The parser builds the value
after it has read the whole command line, so a subcommand that was not chosen never exists, and
a field that the command line does not give takes its `Opt.default`, its environment variable,
or `ArgValue.initial`.

Subcommands are the variants of a union, named in kebab case: a field marked with
`Command.subcommand` holds the variant that the command line chose.

The parser accepts `--name value`, `--name=value`, `-n value`, `-n5`, flags such as `--loud`,
grouped one-letter flags such as `-abc`, positional arguments, and `--`, after which every
argument is positional. An option that takes one value, or a flag, may be given once; a
`List` field takes each occurrence. An unknown option names the closest option, when one is
close. `--help` and `-h` give
[`Parsed.Help`](#Parsed.Help), and `--version` gives [`Parsed.Version`](#Parsed.Version) when the command has a version.

Import as `Cli` with `import silk.cli.parse { Cli }`.

<a id="Cli.impl.parse"></a>

### Associated function `parse`

```silk
pub effect fn parse<T: CommandLine>(arguments: &[string]) -> Parsed<T>
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Parses `arguments` into a `T`, as `T`'s `CommandLine` description says. `arguments[0]` is
the program name and is skipped.

#### Details

Each field of `T` is an option unless the description marks it positional or a subcommand.
A description that names a field `T` does not have, or a field type without `ArgValue`, is a
compile error.

<a id="Cli.impl.parseWith"></a>

### Associated function `parseWith`

```silk
pub effect fn parseWith<T: CommandLine>(
    arguments: &[string],
    environment: &[Variable<'_>],
  ) -> Parsed<T>
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Parses like [`Cli.parse`](#Cli.impl.parse), and reads an option that the command line does not give from
`environment` when the option names a variable with `Opt.env`. The command line wins over the
environment, and the environment wins over `Opt.default`.

<a id="Cli.impl.parseBytes"></a>

### Associated function `parseBytes`

```silk
pub effect fn parseBytes<T: CommandLine>(
    arguments: &[Bytes],
    environment: &[Variable<'_>],
  ) -> Parsed<T>
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Parses like [`Cli.parseWith`](#Cli.impl.parseWith), from arguments as the program received them, such as
`HostInput.arguments`. A `Bytes` field takes its argument's exact bytes; every other field
reads the argument as text, where each byte that is not valid UTF-8 reads as `?`.

<a id="Cli.impl.fromHost"></a>

### Associated function `fromHost`

```silk
pub effect fn fromHost<T: CommandLine>() -> Parsed<T>
    ! HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut HostInput | &mut Allocator
```

Reads the process arguments, and the environment variables that `T`'s description names,
and parses them with [`Cli.parseWith`](#Cli.impl.parseWith).

#### Errors

- `HostInputError` if the arguments cannot be read.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the copies.

<a id="Cli.impl.read"></a>

### Associated function `read`

```silk
pub effect fn read<T: CommandLine>() -> Result<T, i32>
    ! HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError | WriterError
    ? &mut HostInput | &mut Allocator
```

Reads the command line like [`Cli.fromHost`](#Cli.impl.fromHost), and handles everything but a value: it writes
the help text or the version to standard output, or the error to standard error. Returns the
value, or in `Result.Failure` the exit code for `main` to return: 0 after help or the
version, 2 after an error.

#### Errors

- `HostInputError` if the arguments cannot be read.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the copies.
- `WriterError` if standard output or standard error fails.

```silk
    ! WriterError

```

Writes the help text of the command or subcommand at `path` (from [`Parsed.Help`](#Parsed.Help); empty
for the root command) of `T`.

#### Errors

- `WriterError` if the `Writer` fails.
